title: How thick does a thin sheet get after seventeen folds?
description: A sheet of paper is doubled fold after fold, and the thickness is written down for one, two, three, ten and seventeen folds. Keeko's doubt is that seventeen folds make the sheet only seventeen times as thick.
teaching_notes: One idea: each fold multiplies the thickness by two, so the thickness doubles again and again instead of growing by the same amount. Watch for students who add the thickness once per fold.

source: A sheet is 0.001 cm thick. Find its thickness after 1, 2, 3,
video_script.why: The child has met the idea of folding and now sees how the thickness is found fold by fold.
video_script.substitution: The book's own sheet, zero point zero zero one centimetres thick, folded again and again.
video_script.anchor: a thin sheet of paper drawn side on, folded in half again and again
video_script.wrong_answer: zero point zero one seven centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the thickness of one sheet by the number of folds, so seventeen folds give seventeen sheets. A fold doubles the layers, so ten folds already pass one centimetre.
video_script.payoff_line: After seventeen folds, the sheet is about one hundred thirty one centimetres thick

final_answer.value: 0.002 cm, 0.004 cm, 0.008 cm, 1.024 cm and about 131 cm
final_answer.spoken: zero point zero zero two, zero point zero zero four, zero point zero zero eight, one point zero two four and about one hundred thirty one centimetres

never_show: the number of folds that reaches the Moon
maths_rules: 4 folds 0.016, 5 folds 0.032, 6 folds 0.064, 7 folds 0.128, 8 folds 0.256, 9 folds 0.512, 10 folds 1.024 cm
slip: 17 × 0.001 = 0.017 cm adds layers instead of doubling them
video_script.design: One idea: each fold doubles the thickness. The thin sheet seen from the side stays all video; the doubling table grows fold by fold; one slip at the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about folding paper.
<bookmark mark='sheet'/>A sheet of paper is zero point zero zero one centimetres thick.
Each fold doubles its thickness.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How thick is the sheet after one, two, three, ten and seventeen folds?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the sheet side on as one thin layer; a fold lays it over itself and two layers show

marks.side: the sheet is drawn as one thin layer
marks.fold: the sheet folds over and two layers show

narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>Look at the sheet from the side, as one thin layer.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>A fold lays the sheet over itself, so two layers sit where one sat before.
The thickness doubles.

beats.on_screen: Given: thickness 0.001 cm; each fold doubles it

marks.given: the thickness and the doubling are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the sheet is zero point zero zero one centimetres thick, and each fold doubles the thickness.

beats.on_screen: To find: thickness after 1, 2, 3, 10 and 17 folds

marks.find: the five fold counts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the thickness after one, two, three, ten and seventeen folds.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, one fold doubles the thickness, so multiply by two.
Zero point zero zero one times two gives zero point zero zero two centimetres.

marks.two: the thickness is doubled once more
marks.three: the thickness is doubled a third time

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, the second fold doubles that again, and so does the third.
Zero point zero zero two times two is zero point zero zero four.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Zero point zero zero four times two is zero point zero zero eight centimetres.

beats.on_screen: table: 4 folds 0.016 cm, 5 folds 0.032, 6 folds 0.064, 7 folds 0.128, 8 folds 0.256, 9 folds 0.512, 10 folds 1.024 cm

marks.ten: the table fills down to ten folds
marks.four: the rows for four folds and ten folds light up

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Step three, keep doubling, fold after fold, as the table in your book does.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four folds give zero point zero one six, and ten folds give one point zero two four centimetres.

marks.seventeen: the table continues to sixteen folds and the last doubling is shown

narration: <bookmark mark='seventeen'/>Step four, seven more doublings take ten folds to seventeen folds.
Sixteen folds give sixty five point five three six centimetres, and the next fold doubles it.

marks.ans2: the next two thicknesses are boxed
marks.ans3: the ten fold thickness is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>One fold gives zero point zero zero two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Two folds give zero point zero zero four, and three folds give zero point zero zero eight.
<bookmark mark='ans3'/>Ten folds give one point zero two four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ans4'/>After seventeen folds, the sheet is about one hundred thirty one centimetres thick.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the table
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 0.017 cm appears, then is crossed out; the layers double on each fold

marks.doubt: 0.017 cm appears next to the sheet
marks.fix: 0.017 cm is crossed out and the layers double fold after fold

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the sheet is zero point zero one seven centimetres thick, because seventeen folds make seventeen sheets.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a fold doubles the layers, it does not add one more sheet.
That is why ten folds already give more than one centimetre.
